# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — EMPTY SEED: created prompt.md + task_template.md; killed the "file exists = done" default, made inspect→write→verify an ordered procedure, and stopped the pandas whole-sheet round-trip

Baseline val 0.600 (24/40). `prompt.md` was 0 bytes, `task_template.md` did not exist — the
agent ran on the adapter's default first-user-message and NO system prompt. Both files created.

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file + cluster):
  - `prompt.md` "FACT 1" — output contract + worked openpyxl-in-place example, for the
    **pandas `read_excel`→`to_excel` whole-sheet round-trip** cluster (10 failing tasks:
    341-40, 535-20, 48924, 55817, 5835, 44913, 42354, 51359, 38985, 46646). Names the mechanism
    (retypes text→int/date, shifts rows via header/index, drops other sheets, writes NaN /
    `Unnamed: 3`) rather than just forbidding it.
  - `prompt.md` "FACT 2" — two NARROW additive rules: never write an array/CSE formula as a
    plain string (33722), and never write a formula that can resolve to `#DIV/0!`/`#N/A`
    (53647, 42354). Explicitly does NOT ban formulas.
  - `prompt.md` value-contract block — real typed values / text stays text (341-40, 535-20);
    blank means `None` not `""` (44913, 42354, 53647); precision applies to the STORED value
    (46646, 49036, 11842).
  - `prompt.md` closing section — recovery guidance: `[Code executed successfully with no
    output]` means SUCCESS, and "change the approach, not the whitespace", for the
    **30-rounds-of-identical-resubmission** cluster (7 tasks; 25–27 byte-identical blocks each).
  - `task_template.md` — **DELETED** the default's "once that file exists, you are done" and
    replaced it with "finishing fast is worth nothing, only the cell values are scored".
  - `task_template.md` Steps 1–4 — ordered procedure: Step 1 inspection-only (no writing
    `output_path` in the first block), Step 2 compute+write, Step 3 MANDATORY re-open the
    written file and print coordinate/repr/type over answer_position + a 5-item checklist,
    Step 4 finish gated on Step 3 being clean. Targets the two cross-cutting clusters:
    38/40 tasks wrote the graded file blind in round 1, and 0/40 ever verified it.
  - `task_template.md` Step 1 addenda — print the cells a formula/lookup REFERENCES, and
    confirm any literal label you match on actually occurs in the column you search
    (379-36: the quoted label "Georgia Its Tax" is the column-K HEADER; column E holds Payee,
    so its `==` test matched nothing and the range came back byte-identical; 41978, 11842).
  - `task_template.md` interaction contract — **only the FIRST python fence in a reply is
    executed, later ones are discarded unrun**. Verified in traces: 41978 (3 blocks) and 5835
    (2 blocks) both put their verification block second and lost it; 0 passing tasks do this.
  - `task_template.md` field semantics — Sheet-Level `answer_position` is a permission BUDGET,
    not a fill target (341-40 changed 955 cells it was merely allowed to touch; 535-20, 379-36).

- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why it's safe: every edit above is ADDITIVE or a
  clarification of a contract the 24 passers already satisfy, EXCEPT the cluster-1 method
  preference, which I declare UNBOUNDED in PROCESS.md. I read all 13 passing `to_excel` users:
  the multi-sheet ones (13-1, 297-42, 18645, 47827, 58147) already reproduce every sheet via
  `ExcelWriter` — the escape hatch the rule states — and for the single-sheet ones
  openpyxl-in-place writes the same values while additionally preserving untouched cells, so
  it cannot turn a correct cell incorrect. Verification/inspection edits add rounds and prints;
  they cannot change a correct value into a wrong one.
- Checked and did NOT do: ban formulas. 42198 PASSES writing only `=IF(COUNTIFS(...))` strings,
  which proves the scorer recalculates formulas — a formula ban would have regressed 31011,
  39515, 41589, 42198, 49801, 52807, 55468. This is the single most important thing for the
  next iteration not to undo.

- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist — iteration 1, `prior_iterations/` and `RUNMAP.md`
  empty, `rejected.jsonl` empty. Nothing to avoid re-trying yet.
- Refuted hypotheses: none proven by a RESULT yet. One hypothesis I refuted from the traces
  myself (not from a RESULT): "failures are caused by writing formulas instead of values" —
  false, see 42198 above.
- ENVIRONMENT fault: NONE. `rollout.error` is None on all 40 tasks; no repeated infra error;
  the only import failure in the set (11842's own bad `openpyxl.worksheet.formula` import) was
  self-corrected the next round. All 16 failures are genuine capability failures.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: the single-cell near-misses 11842 (1 of 96 cells) and
  49036 (percent-format rendering), and 379-36's under-determined "whole number vs pennies"
  intent. I deliberately did not add task-shaped wording for these — it would overfit and risk
  the precision-sensitive passers.
- Plateau signal: none yet (first iteration). If this candidate is REJECTED, the highest-value
  suspect to drop FIRST is the cluster-1 openpyxl-in-place *method* preference (the one
  UNBOUNDED edit) while KEEPING the Step 1/Step 3 inspect+verify procedure, the first-block-only
  rule, and the deletion of "once that file exists, you are done" — those are additive and
  independently evidenced.
- Focus next iteration: read the RESULT to see whether the method switch or the procedure drove
  the move; then attack the precision/rendering cluster (46646, 49036, 11842) with a worked
  example rather than more prose.

### Addendum to cand_0001 (findings that arrived from the parallel diagnostic subagents after the entry above, and the edits they added)
- **SHEET-NAME KILL — the strongest single finding, and I reproduced it end-to-end.**
  `pd.read_excel(p, sheet_name='Query')` → `df.to_excel(out)` turns `['Sheet1','Query']` into
  `['Sheet1']`. When `answer_position` names a sheet, the grader cannot find it and scores 0
  **without comparing any value**. This explains the signature that had puzzled me on 42354 and
  51359: full matching coverage and NO MISMATCH line at all. Added as the first bullet under
  FACT 1 in `prompt.md` plus checklist item 4 in `task_template.md` ("the sheet named in
  answer_position is still in chk.sheetnames"). Affects 42354, 51359, 5835.
- **Premature ROUNDING, not formatting** (46646: `round(v,9)` left only 2 of 12 values correct;
  49036: `f"{x:.0%} WIN RATE"`). Replaced my weaker "respect the stated precision" line with two
  sharper ones: wording about decimals/commas describes a **number format**, not the value —
  don't round unless asked to round the value; and decide explicitly whether a percent cell
  holds `0.67` or `67` by looking at the neighbours you printed.
- **Only the FIRST ```python fence in a reply is executed; later fences are discarded unrun.**
  41978 (3 fences) and 5835 (2 fences) each put their verification block second and lost it.
  0 passing tasks emit multiple fences. Added to the interaction contract — this is what makes
  Step 1 and Step 3 genuinely separate rounds instead of two blocks in one reply.
- **CORRECTION to my cluster 4 above, from checking the control group.** I had ranked
  "30 rounds of identical resubmission" as a failure cluster. It is mostly a harness artifact:
  **11 PASSING tasks churn identically** (30-round churn = 11 passing vs 7 failing), because the
  loop-break never fires while each block keeps re-saving the output. I therefore kept only the
  3 cheap additive sentences and did NOT build a procedure around it. A future iteration should
  NOT spend effort trying to stop the churn — it is not correlated with failure.
- Lesson for the next iteration, in one line: **compute every candidate signal over the PASSING
  set too.** That control is what demoted the churn cluster and what stopped me from banning
  formulas (42198 passes on formula strings alone).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.850 Δ=+0.250 · fixed={33722, 379-36, 38985, 41978, 42354, 44913, 48924, 51359, 53647, 55817} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## SpreadsheetBench scorer semantics (what the graded artifact actually is)
- What worked (no RESULT yet — this is trace-verified, not gate-verified): **the scorer
  recalculates Excel formulas before comparing.** Task 42198 scores 1.0 with a final program
  that only ever writes `=IF(COUNTIFS(...))` strings via openpyxl and never computes a value.
  Corollary a future iteration must not undo: do NOT instruct the agent to always write literal
  values instead of formulas — 7 passing tasks (31011, 39515, 41589, 42198, 49801, 52807, 55468)
  pass by writing formulas.
- The real formula defects are narrower than "formulas": (a) **array/CSE formulas** written as
  plain strings evaluate against a single cell, not the array (33722, all 5 cells wrong);
  (b) formulas that can resolve to `#DIV/0!`/`#N/A` are stored as **error text** and never
  equal an expected number (53647, 42354).
- What didn't: n/a (no RESULT yet).
- Promising but not yet tried: the precision/rendering cluster (46646's 0/1/9-decimal rule,
  49036's integer-percent-plus-text, 11842's 1-of-96 near-miss) is untouched by general prose
  and probably needs a worked example of stored-value-vs-number-format.

## SpreadsheetBench agent behavior under the as-shipped default prompt
- Measured over all 40 val trajectories (scripted, reproducible): **38/40 tasks write the graded
  output file in their very first code block**, before any real cell value has been observed;
  only 6/40 tasks ever call `print(`; **0/40 ever re-open `output_path` to check what they
  wrote**; and 16/40 burn all 30 rounds re-sending 25–27 byte-identical blocks. The cause is
  structural, not a knowledge gap: every block ends in a silent `wb.save(...)`, so the harness
  returns `[Code executed successfully with no output]`, which the agent reads as "nothing
  happened" and retries verbatim.
- **Adapter mechanic worth remembering: only the FIRST ```python fence in a reply is executed;
  later fences are discarded unrun.** 41978 (3 fences) and 5835 (2 fences) each put their
  verification block second and silently lost it. Zero passing tasks emit multiple fences.
- `pd.read_excel` → `df.to_excel` is the dominant failure mechanism (10 of 16 failures). It
  regenerates the whole sheet: text→int/date coercion, one-row shifts from header/index
  mismatch, other sheets dropped, `NaN`/`Unnamed: 3` written into cells. The scorer names it
  directly: *"N cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original
  input"* and *"int where str was expected — KEEP the original text"*.

## The sheet-name kill (pandas to_excel silently renames the sheet) — REPRODUCED
- Confirmed by direct reproduction, not inference: `pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name='Query')`
  returns a DataFrame that no longer carries its sheet name, so `df.to_excel(out)` writes ONE
  sheet named `Sheet1`. Input `['Sheet1','Query']` → output `['Sheet1']`. When `answer_position`
  names a sheet, the grader looks it up, fails, and scores 0 **before comparing any value** —
  so the agent's numbers can be entirely correct and still score zero.
- **Diagnostic signature to recognize it in feedback:** full/matching COVERAGE counts and **no
  MISMATCH line at all**. That combination means the scorer never got as far as comparing cells.
  Present on 42354 and 51359; 5835 also round-trips a named sheet (`גיליון1`).
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing else needed here — the fix is the openpyxl-in-place idiom
  plus asserting `answer_position`'s sheet is still in `sheetnames` of the file you wrote.

## Round-cap churn is NOT a failure signal (control-group check)
- 30-round churn (61-message trajectories with 25–27 byte-identical consecutive blocks) occurs
  on **11 PASSING tasks vs 7 failing** ones. It is a harness artifact: the loop-break never
  fires while each resubmitted block keeps re-saving the output file. Do NOT spend an iteration
  trying to stop the churn — it is uncorrelated with reward.
- The generalizable method lesson: **compute every candidate failure signal over the PASSING set
  before ranking it.** This control demoted the churn cluster, and the same control (42198
  passing on formula strings alone) prevented a formula ban that would have regressed 7 tasks.

## Premature rounding vs number format
- 46646 applied `round(v, 9)` to full-precision floats and only 2 of 12 values survived; 49036
  wrote `f"{x:.0%} WIN RATE"` as a string. Instruction wording about decimal places, commas, or
  what to "show" describes the **number format** (display); the stored value stays exact, and the
  grader reads the stored value. Round only when the instruction asks for a rounded *value*.

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far — first and, per the budget, possibly only iteration)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: EMPTY-SEED creation of both prompt files at once,
  covering 9 clusters in one candidate. No LEDGER row yet to cite — this is iteration 1 and the
  framework stamps the RESULT after I stop.
- What actually produced the diagnosis (the transferable part): **scripted cross-trace counting
  beat reading traces one by one.** Five one-off scripts over the 40 trajectory JSONs produced
  the whole ranking in minutes and, more importantly, produced the *control* group each time:
  - `round-1 writes output_path` → 38/40 (so "blind write" is the base behavior, not a quirk)
  - `print(` appears anywhere → 6/40 tasks
  - byte-identical consecutive blocks → 25–27 on every round-cap task
  - `to_excel` vs openpyxl `.save` crossed with reward → 10 of 16 failures vs the passers
  - multiple ```python fences in one reply → exactly 2 tasks, both FAILING, 0 passing
  The pattern worth repeating: **always compute the same statistic over the PASSING set.** It is
  what turned "formulas are the problem" into "formulas are fine, 42198 passes on formulas
  alone" — and that single control saved me from shipping a formula ban that would have
  regressed 7 passing tasks.
- Where the subagents helped and where they didn't: two parallel read-only diagnostic subagents
  were worth it for ONE thing I would not have scripted — the harness's first-fence-only code
  extraction (41978, 5835 lost their verification block). I then verified that claim myself in
  30 seconds. Their per-task narratives otherwise duplicated my scripted clustering. Next time:
  spawn fewer, and brief them to hunt for *harness/adapter mechanics* rather than to re-describe
  each failure, since the mechanics are what a script cannot see.
- Stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to: none yet (no prior RESULTs to be flat
  against). The structural risk I accepted instead: 8 of 9 clusters got BOUNDED additive edits,
  but cluster 1 needed an UNBOUNDED *method* switch (prefer openpyxl-in-place over pandas
  round-trip) touching 13 passing tasks. I kept it because it is value-preserving by
  construction, but it is the one edit that can sink the candidate, and it is named as the
  first thing to drop in JOURNAL.md if the RESULT is REJECTED.
- What to try next iteration: read the RESULT first to attribute the move between (a) the
  method switch and (b) the inspect/verify procedure — they are confounded in this candidate,
  which is the main methodological weakness of shipping 9 clusters at once. If val moved a lot,
  leave both and attack the precision/rendering cluster (46646, 49036, 11842) with a worked
  example. If val moved barely, the procedure is probably being skipped despite being ordered,
  and the lever to switch to is a worked end-to-end example of a full 3-round session rather
  than more imperative steps.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From the SpreadsheetBench empty-seed run (cand_0001)
- **The adapter's default task template actively causes a failure cluster, and it is not in the
  edit space until you overwrite it.** The shipped default ends with "once that file exists,
  you are done" — an instruction to stop at file-existence rather than correct values. On an
  EMPTY SEED the optimizer only discovers this by noticing that `trace[0]` of every trajectory
  contains text that exists in no file in the working directory. Suggestion: on an empty seed,
  write the adapter's current effective default into the capability files (or into a
  `baseline_prompt_as_shipped.md`) so the optimizer can see and diff what the agent is really
  reading, instead of reconstructing it from traces.
- **Harness mechanics that silently change agent behavior should be documented to the
  optimizer.** This adapter executes only the FIRST ```python fence in a reply and discards the
  rest unrun; two failing tasks lost their verification block that way. Nothing in
  INSTRUCTIONS.md or the guidance mentions it, and no prose edit can be aimed at it until the
  optimizer reverse-engineers it from traces. A short "adapter contract" note (how code is
  extracted, how many blocks run, what the no-output message means, whether formulas are
  recalculated before scoring) would be high value and cost the framework nothing.
- **Please expose the scorer's comparison semantics.** I had to infer from one passing task
  (42198, which passes writing only formula strings) that the scorer RECALCULATES formulas. If
  I had guessed the other way — the intuitive guess, since openpyxl writes no cached value — I
  would have shipped a formula ban and regressed 7 passing tasks. That is a coin-flip the
  framework could remove with one sentence.
- **`{max_turns}` is listed as optional but the round budget is load-bearing.** Several failures
  are round-exhaustion; the optimizer needs to know the real cap to decide how many rounds a
  procedure may safely spend. Worth making it non-optional, or stating the value in INSTRUCTIONS.
- **Minor:** `PROCESS.md`'s ranked-issue table asks for a tag from {KNOWLEDGE, BEHAVIORAL,
  DECISION/PERMISSION, CAPABILITY-GAP}, while the prose levers section uses
  CONTRACT/STRUCTURE/KNOWLEDGE/DECISION. The two vocabularies don't map onto each other
  cleanly (an output-contract miss is arguably both KNOWLEDGE and CONTRACT). Picking one
  taxonomy would make cross-iteration PROCESS files comparable.

# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

EMPTY SEED iteration. `prompt.md` was 0 bytes and `task_template.md` did not exist. The agent
was running on the adapter's built-in default first-user-message only (visible verbatim as
`trace[0]` in every trajectory) and **no system prompt at all**. I created both files.

Baseline: val 0.600 — 24 pass / 16 fail of 40.

## What the baseline agent was actually reading

`trace[0]` of every trajectory is the adapter default. Two properties of it drive most failures:

- It ends with **"once that file exists, you are done"** — an explicit instruction to stop at
  file-existence rather than at correct values. This is the anti-pattern the task brief warns
  about, and it is in the shipped default.
- It describes the fields but states **no output contract** (no typing rule, no "don't touch
  cells outside the range", no formula guidance) and **no procedure**.

Measured consequences across all 40 traces (I scripted these counts, they are not impressions):

| signal | count |
| --- | --- |
| tasks whose **round-1** block already writes `output_path` (zero inspection) | **38 / 40** |
| assistant blocks containing `print(` anywhere | **6 / 40 tasks** |
| execution results that are `[Code executed successfully with no output]` | **~29 / 30 rounds** on every long task |
| tasks that burn all 30 rounds re-sending a **byte-identical** block (25–27 dups) | 16 |

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)

| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **pandas round-trip destroys the file** | 341-40, 535-20, 48924, 55817, 5835, 44913, 42354, 51359, 38985, 46646 (10) | `pd.read_excel` → `df.to_excel` regenerates the whole sheet: coerces text→int/date, shifts rows via header/index, drops other sheets, writes `NaN`/`Unnamed: 3`. Scorer says so literally: *"955 cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input"*, *"700 cells hold int where str was expected"* | KNOWLEDGE (+CONTRACT) | output contract + worked example (`prompt.md`) |
| 2 | **blind write, never inspects the real grid** | all 16 (38/40 write on round 1) | The `spreadsheet_content` preview shows 5 rows with pandas' invented headers; real sheets have title rows, side-by-side tables, blank leading rows. Agent guesses indices from the preview | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure, inspection as Step 1 precondition (`task_template.md`) |
| 3 | **never verifies the written values** | all 16 | Nothing in the default asks it to re-open the output; "once that file exists, you are done" actively tells it not to. So an off-by-one row offset is never detected | BEHAVIORAL (skipped step) | mandatory Step 3 + explicit checklist (`task_template.md`) |
| 4 | **30 rounds of identical resubmission** — *downgraded, see caveat* | 33722, 48924, 51359, 42354, 46646, 38985, 53647 (7) | Every block ends in a silent `wb.save(...)`, so the result is always `[Code executed successfully with no output]`. The agent reads that as "nothing happened" and resubmits the same code 26×. **CAVEAT I verified: 11 PASSING tasks show the identical churn (30-round churn = 11 passing vs 7 failing).** So the churn is mostly a harness artifact (the loop-break never fires while the block keeps re-saving the output) and is NOT itself a cause of failure. I kept only the cheap, additive part of this fix and did NOT build a procedure around it | KNOWLEDGE + recovery guidance | state what the message means + "change approach, not whitespace" (`prompt.md`) |
| 5 | **array formula written as a plain string** | 33722 | `=MEDIAN(IF($C2:$C$12<=0.01,...))` is a CSE formula; as a plain string it evaluates against one cell → all 5 cells "a different value of the right type" | KNOWLEDGE | narrow additive rule (`prompt.md`) |
| 6 | **formula that resolves to an Excel error** | 53647, 42354 | Scorer: *"1 cell holds an Excel error text — an unresolved formula was written out as its error string"*, *"str where float was expected"* | KNOWLEDGE | narrow additive rule (`prompt.md`) |
| 7 | **blank-cell convention `""` vs empty** | 44913, 42354, 53647 | Wrote `""` into cells the reference leaves genuinely empty; coverage shows *"your output has a value in 12 of them; the expected has 3"* | KNOWLEDGE (+CONTRACT) | one contract line (`prompt.md`) |
| 1b | **SHEET-NAME KILL (subset of cluster 1, distinct mechanism)** | 42354, 51359, 5835 | `pd.read_excel(path, sheet_name='Query')` returns a DataFrame that no longer knows its name, so `to_excel` writes a single sheet called **`Sheet1`**. When `answer_position` names a sheet the grader cannot find it and scores 0 **without comparing any value**. Diagnostic signature, which I confirmed: 42354 and 51359 have full matching coverage and **no MISMATCH line at all** in their feedback | KNOWLEDGE | explicit first bullet under FACT 1 + checklist item 4 |
| 8 | **premature ROUNDING of the stored value** | 46646, 49036, 11842 | Instruction describes *display* (decimal places, commas, "show as") and the agent rounds the **value**. 46646 applied `round(v,9)` and only 2 of 12 values survived; 49036 rendered `f"{x:.0%} WIN RATE"` as a string | KNOWLEDGE | number-format-vs-value contract lines (`prompt.md`) |
| 10 | **multiple code fences in one reply** | 41978, 5835 | Only the FIRST ```python fence is executed; later ones are discarded unrun. Both tasks put their *verification* block second and silently lost it, so they believed they had inspected when they had not. 0 passing tasks emit multiple fences | KNOWLEDGE (adapter mechanic) | interaction-contract line (`task_template.md`) |
| 11 | **matched literal label that is not in the searched column** | 379-36 | The label quoted in the instruction (`"Georgia Its Tax"`) is the column-**K header**; column E holds `Payee`. The `==` test matched nothing, so the range came back byte-identical | BEHAVIORAL | Step 1 addendum: confirm the literal occurs in the column you search |
| 9 | **Sheet-Level range read as a fill target** | 341-40, 535-20, 379-36 | `answer_position` for Sheet-Level is the *maximum permitted* region, not cells to fill. 341-40 rewrote all 955 cells it was merely allowed to touch | KNOWLEDGE | field-semantics line (`task_template.md`) |

**No ENVIRONMENT fault found.** I checked for it explicitly: `rollout.error` is `None` on all
40 tasks, there is no repeated infra error, and the only import failure in the whole set is one
task's own bad import (`from openpyxl.worksheet.formula import Formula` in 11842) which it
self-corrected next round. The 16 failures are genuine capability failures.

## Changes made this iteration

Two files created from scratch. `prompt.md` = system message (facts + output contract);
`task_template.md` = first user message (field semantics + ordered procedure). I chose that
split deliberately: **durable knowledge/contract** goes in the system prompt, **per-task
procedure and the interaction contract** go in the template where the placeholders are, so the
verify snippet can interpolate the task's real `{output_path}`.

| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | tighten output contract + worked example | `prompt.md` "FACT 1" | Names the mechanism (regenerates the file: coerces types, shifts rows, drops sheets) and gives the 5-line openpyxl-in-place idiom. Stated as a *default with a condition* — pandas may still write if you reproduce every sheet and original value | see blast radius below |
| 2 | ordered procedure | `task_template.md` Step 1 | "Your first block only prints. Do not write output_path yet." Inspection is a precondition of Step 2, not advice | yes — additive round |
| 3 | pre-finish checklist | `task_template.md` Step 3 + 5-item list | Re-open the written file, print `coordinate/repr(value)/type` over the answer_position range; Step 4 (finish) is gated on Step 3 printing clean | yes |
| 4 | recovery guidance + knowledge | `prompt.md` last section | States that `[Code executed successfully with no output]` means success, and "change the approach, not the whitespace" | yes |
| 5 | additive narrow rule | `prompt.md` FACT 2 | "Never write an array/CSE formula as a plain string — compute it in Python." Conditioned on array formulas only | yes (no passer writes one) |
| 6 | additive narrow rule | `prompt.md` FACT 2 | "A formula that can resolve to an error is a zero — if it might error on any row, compute in Python" | yes |
| 7 | contract line | `prompt.md` | "Blank means empty: write `None`. Only write `\"\"` if the instruction literally asks for it" | conditioned on the literal ask |
| 8 | contract line | `prompt.md` | "Apply precision to the stored value, not only the display format — the grader reads the stored value" | yes |
| 9 | field semantics | `task_template.md` | Cell-Level = exact cells to fill; Sheet-Level = a **budget**, not a fill target | yes |
| — | role/goal line | `prompt.md` head | "graded by a program… value and type. A beautiful explanation over a wrong cell scores zero" | yes |
| — | **deleted** the harmful default line | `task_template.md` | Removed "once that file exists, you are done" and replaced it with "finishing fast is worth nothing, only the cell values are scored". This is a *deletion of text shown to be counterproductive* — cluster 3 exists because of it. No constraint was lost: the file-writing requirement survives as Step 2 + `output_path` field semantics | yes — it can only add verification |

Improvement types applied, per the capability SKILL's menu: #1 positive rewrite, #2 rule+reason,
#4 sourced additive rule, #5 worked example, #6 restructure, #7 role/goal line, #8 tighten the
output contract — seven of the nine classes, plus the ordered-procedure and recovery levers from
the brief. Not a single lever repeated across clusters.

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)

- **C1 (341-40):** trace writes `df.to_excel(output_path, index=False)` after `pd.read_excel`;
  scorer returns *"700 cells hold the CORRECT value stored as text instead of as a number/date"*
  and *"955 cells were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input"*.
  With FACT 1's openpyxl-in-place idiom the agent assigns only column Q and the other 955 cells
  keep their original stored types — exactly what the scorer says it wanted.
- **C1 (535-20):** `df[cols_to_keep].to_excel(...)` dropped 253 expected values and coerced 4
  str→int; deleting columns via `ws.delete_cols()` in place leaves the rest byte-identical.
- **C1 (5835 / 51359):** `read_excel(header=None)` + `to_excel(header=False)` is the row-shift
  trap; 5835 filled 10 of 17 cells. Addressed by the same in-place idiom.
- **C2 (46646, 38985):** these are the only 2 of 40 that *did* print the grid first — and both
  then needed it (46646's data was on row 8 / col O, nothing like the preview). The other 38
  never printed. Step 1 makes that first print unconditional.
- **C3 (5835):** wrote to `df.iloc[i,2]` for `i in range(2,19)` targeting C3:C19 — a one-row
  offset that produced 7 empty cells. Step 3's `print(c.coordinate, repr(c.value))` over
  `C3:C19` surfaces exactly that; checklist item 1 then sends it back to Step 2. Verified the
  snippet runs: I rendered the template with `.format()`, extracted both code blocks and
  executed them against a synthetic multi-sheet workbook — Step 1 printed the grid and every
  sheet; Step 3 printed `D8 80 int … D11 110 int` plus `SHEETS: ['Sheet1','Data']`.
- **C4 (33722):** 30 blocks, 26 byte-identical to their predecessor, every result
  `[Code executed successfully with no output]`. The new lines tell it that message means
  success and forbid resubmission; Step 3 also converts those silent rounds into informative
  ones, which removes the cause rather than scolding the symptom. **But I checked the control
  group and it disconfirms treating this as a failure cause: 11 passing tasks churn the same
  way.** So this edit is 3 sentences, not a procedure — the expected gain is that Step 3 makes
  the wasted rounds informative, not that churn itself stops.
- **C5 (33722):** wrote `=MEDIAN(IF(($C{row}:$C$12<=0.01)*...))`; all 5 cells wrong. Contract
  now routes array formulas to a Python-computed literal. **Scorer-checked:** 42198 passes
  writing *only* `=IF(COUNTIFS(...))` strings, so formulas ARE recalculated — the defect is
  specifically CSE semantics, not formulas. I did not ban formulas; that would have regressed
  31011, 39515, 41589, 42198, 49801, 52807, 55468.
- **C6 (53647):** `=IF(ISNUMBER(C7), C$3/C7, ...)` → scorer *"1 cell holds an Excel error text
  … str where float was expected"*. Rule routes error-prone formulas to Python values.
- **C7 (44913):** `else ""` → *"your output has a value in 12 of them; the expected output has
  a value in 3"*. `None` produces the 3-value coverage the scorer expects. Conditioned on "only
  if the instruction literally asks for `\"\"`", which is what 44913's own instruction does *not*
  require despite its `blank/empty ("")` phrasing — hence the qualifier rather than a flat rule.
- **C9 (341-40):** Sheet-Level `A1:Q701`; agent treated all 11917 cells as writable and changed
  955. Template now defines Sheet-Level as a permission budget.
- **C1b (42354, 51359) — reproduced end-to-end, the strongest single finding.** I built a
  2-sheet workbook, ran `pd.read_excel(p, sheet_name='Query')` → `df.to_excel(out)` and got
  `input sheets ['Sheet1','Query']` → `output sheets ['Sheet1']`. The named sheet is gone, so
  the grader scores 0 before comparing anything. This explains a signature that had puzzled me:
  42354 and 51359 report *full matching coverage and no MISMATCH line at all*. Both are now
  covered twice over — the first bullet under FACT 1 states the mechanism, and checklist item 4
  makes the agent assert the sheet still exists in the file it wrote.
- **C8 (46646):** applied `round(v, 9)` to full-precision floats; only 2 of 12 values survived
  (10 cells "a different value of the right type"). The contract now separates *number format*
